concept: Primary-driven index builds (spill to a replicated table)

claims.text: SERVER-132662 asks engineers to measure foreground-throughput impact against build duration when choosing scan/load throttles. Its 1.5x build-duration target is a goal, not a reported benchmark result. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-04)

SERVER-112247 records historical test-coverage loss because step-up aborted builds with InterruptedDueToReplStateChange. Later coordinator code includes conditional resumption, so the historical ticket cannot establish universal present-day failover behavior. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-112247 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-125008

SERVER-131721 reports scan-phase tests producing many single-key ci entries after initially batched applyOps, potentially wasting oplog space. The ticket was resolved as Gone away, rather than documenting a quantified performance fix. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-04)

Step-up resumption is conditional: coordinator code checks the resumability flag, build ident and pending interceptors. If resumption does not succeed, it aborts the build rather than unconditionally continuing it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/index_builds/index_builds_coordinator.cpp

In MongoDB's source, when container writes are replicated, an index builder's spills go through replicated container writes and its sorters are released afterward. The bulk builder inserts index keys into an external sorter. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/index_builds/multi_index_block.h

MongoDB's source adds handling to resume in-progress primary-driven index builds on step-up, with separate resume tasks for the initialized, collection-scan, load and drain phases. Builds that cannot be resumed are aborted. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/index_builds/index_builds_coordinator.h ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-125682

During a primary-driven index build, a single-statement retryable write is recorded as an atomically applied applyOps oplog entry containing both the user operation and the index side-write operations. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-129184

In the master source snapshot fetched on 2026-10-20, featureFlagPrimaryDrivenIndexBuilds and featureFlagResumablePrimaryDrivenIndexBuilds both default to false and are FCV-gated. This snapshot does not establish Atlas deployment availability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

SERVER-127648 records a historical race: cleanup delayed past re-election could self-abort a build and destroy its catalog entry. It was closed as a duplicate of SERVER-127769; this is not evidence of an unresolved production defect. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-02)
Primary-driven index builds set the commit quorum to 0 and the server is being changed to skip the commit quorum pathway entirely for them. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-117023

Primary-driven index builds persist a ResumeIndexInfo record to a replicated internal-indexBuild-<UUID> table at the end of the collection scan, periodically during the scan, at the end of the load phase, periodically during the load phase, at the beginning of the drain phase, and when merging spills before deleting old ranges. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-125586

During a primary-driven index build, collection writes and index side writes are applied atomically: a single-statement retryable write produces an applyOps oplog entry with multiOpType 2 (kApplyOpsAppliedAtomically) containing the user operation and the container side write operations. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-129184

In the inspected source snapshot, featureFlagPrimaryDrivenIndexBuilds, featureFlagResumablePrimaryDrivenIndexBuilds and featureFlagContainerWrites each default to false and are FCV-gated. These definitions do not establish Atlas enablement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

The baseline being changed is simultaneous per-node building: Percona's July 7, 2022 walkthrough says that from MongoDB 4.4 onward index builds run simultaneously on all data-bearing nodes. Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-building-on-replicaset-and-shard-cluster/
